audit.whatIsWrong: Level 2 was given to Tahm Kench though its why ends 'keeping it even'; levels 4-5 were scored Skill though the why says he out-sustains the whole window; level 6 was scored Skill though its why calls it 'your one owned window'.
audit.why: 46.11% over 193 games — a losing lane in which Kennen owns exactly one row, the level-6 stun-lock before Tahm Kench has any MR.
audit.corrected: Row 1 -> Skill, row 3 -> Tahm Kench, row 4 -> Kennen, in matched pairs. That is the packet chart.

audit.why: Level 6 is the single Kennen spike and first item is where Tahm Kench takes it back — the spikes had that right; only the mechanics inside them were wrong.
audit.corrected: Abyssal Dive's 21s and Tongue Lash's 7s written in.

audit.whatIsWrong: Devour is called W in five fields ('W-devour', 'W devours your squishy body', 'percent-HP W', 'his W reactivate'), the grey-health mechanic is credited to his passive, and Tongue Lash is described as a flat long stun.
audit.why: Riot's kit: P is An Acquired Taste (bonus damage from total health; damaging champions builds stacks). Q Tongue Lash damages, slows and heals him, applies a stack, and STUNS only if the target already has 3 stacks — consuming them. W is Abyssal Dive, a 1000-1200 range dive that knocks up, 21s at rank 1. E Thick Skin is the grey health: it stores a percent of damage taken, heals it back out of combat, and can be converted into a shield on a 3s cooldown. R is Devour, and it needs 3 stacks. There is no percent-health damage anywhere in the kit.
audit.corrected: Slots corrected throughout; the stun restated as stack-gated; grey health attributed to Thick Skin; percent-HP claims removed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing told the reader that Tongue Lash's stun and Devour compete for the same resource.
audit.why: Both consume three stacks of An Acquired Taste, so he gets one or the other, not both. That means counting HIS stacks on you is the actual lane skill — at two stacks neither threat exists, and the tongue is just a slow.
audit.corrected: Stated in early, spikes[2] and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never says how he answers Slicing Maelstrom.
audit.why: The storm is only 550 radius. Tahm Kench's answer is distance — he walks out of it rather than trading inside — which is why the level-6 window has to start with a stun, not with the ult.

edits.before: Tahm Kench's grey-health passive is the whole problem early — your Q chip and Electrical Surge on-hit just turn into grey HP that he heals back, so you almost never reach a third Mark of the Storm stack to stun him. At levels 2-3 you can land a fast double-mark off Q plus W and force him off the wave, but do NOT step into Q-tongue range to do it: his Q is a long stun that interrupts your mark setup, and if it lands he flips into W-devour and bursts your squishy body. Poke from the very edge of Q range, respect the tongue, and accept this is a farm-and-chip lane, not a kill lane.
edits.after: Thick Skin (E) is the whole problem early — your Q chip and Electrical Surge on-hit turn into grey health he regenerates out of combat or converts straight into a shield, so you rarely reach a third Mark of the Storm stack. At levels 2-3 you can land a fast double-mark off Q plus W and force him off the wave, but count HIS stacks while you do it: Tongue Lash only stuns at three stacks of An Acquired Taste, and at three he can spend them to Devour you instead. Poke from the very edge of 950 range, keep his stacks off you, and accept this is a farm-and-chip lane rather than a kill lane.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are a respect stretch — your poke edge means nothing against his grey health and he's already a fat drain-tank, so don't commit. Level 6 is your one real window: Slicing Maelstrom plus the Q-W-E-Flash-R chain stun-locks him and burns through his HP before W and grey health can answer, and he has no MR yet. If you're going to win this lane, win it on this spike or in a 6+ 2v2 dive — bait his Q tongue first, then E in and R only once it's down.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are a respect stretch — your poke edge means nothing against stored grey health and he is already enormous, so don't commit. Level 6 is your one real window: Slicing Maelstrom plus the Q-W-E-Flash-R chain stun-locks him and burns his HP before Thick Skin and Abyssal Dive can answer, and he has no MR yet. If you win this lane, win it on this spike or in a 6+ 2v2 dive — bait Tongue Lash first, then E in and R once it is down.

edits.before: This is where Tahm Kench takes the lane back outright. Once he has Spirit Visage and a single MR or HP item, his percent-HP W and drain-tank sustain shrug off your Hextech Alternator burst, and the moment your R is on cooldown he Q-stuns and devours your squishy frame for free. Don't try to out-duel him in a sidelane — pivot to a teamfight engager, use your AoE R and global presence to peel and start fights for your carries, and let your team handle the unkillable blob.
edits.after: This is where Tahm Kench takes the lane back outright. Once he has Spirit Visage and a single MR or HP item, his health-scaled damage and stored grey health shrug off your Alternator burst, and the moment your R is down three stacks let him stun or Devour your frame for free. Remember Slicing Maelstrom is only 550 radius — he answers it by walking out. Don't out-duel him in a sidelane; pivot to a teamfight engager and let your team handle the blob.

notes: The mirror's finding held here too: Devour is R and requires three An Acquired Taste stacks, and Tongue Lash stuns only at three stacks and consumes them — so the two threats are mutually exclusive and counting stacks is the real lane skill. This page called Devour 'W' in five fields, credited grey health to his passive instead of Thick Skin (E), and invented percent-health damage on W (Abyssal Dive has none; it is a 1000-1200 range dive that knocks up on 21s). Also added the mirror's second point: the answer to Slicing Maelstrom is distance, since the storm is only 550 radius. The mirror notes this Q-stun boilerplate is repeated across Tahm Kench's whole top-lane set — worth a global sweep outside this slice.
